rules.name: Addition principle for disjoint cases
preconditions: The cases are disjoint
rules.operation: Count total outcomes by summing disjoint case counts.
examples: Choosing from two disjoint groups of sizes 3 and 5 yields 8 total choices
counterexamples: Summing overlapping cases without correcting overlap is invalid

rules.name: Multiplication principle
preconditions: The number of second-step choices is well-defined for each first-step choice under the stated model
rules.operation: Count composite outcomes by multiplying counts of sequential choice stages.
examples: 3 shirts and 4 pants give 12 outfits
counterexamples: Using ab when the second-step count changes with the first-step choice is invalid without refinement

rules.name: Mathematical induction pattern
rules.output_form: statement for all integers in range
preconditions: A valid base case is proved
A valid inductive implication is proved
rules.operation: Use induction to extend a proposition from the base case across the intended integer domain.
examples: Induction proves sum_{i=1}^{n} i = n(n+1)/2
counterexamples: Proving only the inductive step without a base case is invalid

rules.name: Inclusion-exclusion for two sets
preconditions: All relevant set cardinalities are finite
rules.operation: Correct double counting in a two-set union by subtracting the overlap once.
examples: If |A| = 5, |B| = 6, and |A intersection B| = 2, then |A union B| = 9
counterexamples: Adding |A| and |B| without subtracting overlap is invalid

rules.name: Pigeonhole principle
rules.output_form: at least one repeated box occupancy
preconditions: Object count exceeds box count
rules.operation: Infer repeated occupancy from excess objects over boxes.
examples: More than 12 objects placed into 12 boxes forces some box to contain at least two objects
counterexamples: Applying the strict-more-than form when object count equals box count is invalid

rules.name: Handshake lemma
preconditions: The graph is finite and undirected
rules.operation: Count each edge twice across vertex degrees.
examples: A graph with 5 edges has total degree sum 10
counterexamples: Odd total degree sum in a finite undirected graph is invalid

rules.name: Recurrence verification rule
rules.input_form: candidate closed form and recurrence system
preconditions: The recurrence and initial conditions are explicit
rules.operation: Validate a candidate sequence by checking both the recurrence relation and initial data.
examples: Checking both recurrence relation and seed values validates the candidate sequence
counterexamples: Matching the recurrence but missing the initial condition is insufficient

rules.name: Binomial coefficient counting rule
rules.output_form: number of k-element subsets of an n-element set
rules.operation: Interpret the binomial coefficient as an unordered selection count.
examples: C(5,2) = 10 counts unordered pairs from 5 objects
counterexamples: Using permutations when order is irrelevant is invalid

rules.name: Pascal identity
rules.operation: Split k-subsets by whether they contain a distinguished element.
counterexamples: Shifting the wrong lower index in Pascal's identity is invalid

rules.name: Tree edge count rule
preconditions: The graph is a tree
rules.operation: Count edges in a finite tree from the tree characterization.
examples: A tree on 7 vertices has 6 edges
counterexamples: A connected graph with cycles can have more than n - 1 edges

rules.name: Connected acyclic graph criterion
preconditions: Connectivity and acyclicity are both determined
rules.operation: Classify a finite undirected graph as a tree exactly when it is connected and acyclic.
examples: Checking both connectivity and absence of cycles certifies a tree
counterexamples: Acyclic but disconnected graphs are forests, not trees

rules.name: Euler formula for connected planar graphs
preconditions: A planar embedding exists and the graph is connected
rules.operation: Relate vertices, edges, and faces through Euler's planar formula.
examples: Planar embeddings obey the Euler characteristic relation 2
counterexamples: Applying the formula to a nonplanar graph without a planar embedding is invalid

rules.name: Ordinary generating function encoding rule
preconditions: A formal power-series context is active
rules.operation: Encode a sequence as its ordinary generating function.
examples: The constant-one sequence has generating function 1 + x + x^2 + ... in formal-series context
counterexamples: Treating a formal generating function as automatically convergent analytically is invalid

rules.name: Proper vertex coloring rule
preconditions: The graph is finite and the coloring is defined on every vertex
rules.operation: Classify a coloring as proper exactly when adjacent vertices receive different colors.
examples: A bipartite graph has a proper coloring with at most two colors
counterexamples: Assigning one color to both ends of an edge is invalid in a proper coloring

rules.name: Bipartite graph criterion by two-colorability
preconditions: The graph is finite
rules.operation: Recognize bipartite graphs through the existence of a proper two-coloring.
examples: Even cycles are bipartite because their vertices alternate between two color classes
counterexamples: An odd cycle is not bipartite and cannot be properly 2-colored

rules.name: Hall marriage criterion seed
rules.input_form: bipartite graph with left part U
rules.output_form: matching saturating U when every S subseteq U satisfies |N(S)| >= |S|
preconditions: The graph is bipartite and Hall's neighborhood condition is checked for every subset of U
rules.operation: Use Hall's neighborhood condition as a seed criterion for existence of a matching saturating one side.
examples: Neighborhood expansion conditions certify the existence of a perfect matching on one side
counterexamples: Checking Hall's condition only for single vertices is invalid in general

rules.name: Max-flow min-cut seed
rules.input_form: capacitated network with source s and sink t
rules.output_form: maximum flow value equals minimum cut capacity
preconditions: A directed capacitated network model is fixed
rules.operation: Connect flow optimization to cut certificates through the max-flow min-cut principle.
examples: Flow optimization can be certified by a cut of the same value
counterexamples: Comparing a flow value to an arbitrary partition that is not an s-t cut is invalid

rules.name: Clique lower bound on chromatic number
preconditions: Clique number and chromatic number are interpreted in the standard graph-theoretic sense
rules.operation: Lower-bound the chromatic number by the size of a largest clique.
examples: A triangle subgraph forces at least three colors in any proper coloring
counterexamples: Concluding equality of clique number and chromatic number for every graph is invalid

rules.name: Planar graph edge bound
rules.input_form: simple connected planar graph with V >= 3
preconditions: The graph is simple, connected, planar, and has at least three vertices
rules.operation: Bound edge count in a simple connected planar graph using Euler-type planar structure.
examples: The planar edge bound quickly rules out some dense graphs from being planar
counterexamples: Applying the bound to multigraphs or to graphs without the stated hypotheses is invalid

rules.name: Adjacency-matrix walk-count rule
rules.input_form: adjacency matrix A and integer k >= 1
rules.output_form: (i,j) entry of A^k counts k-step walks from i to j
preconditions: A is the adjacency matrix of the graph
k is a positive integer
rules.operation: Interpret matrix powers combinatorially as walk counts in the graph.
examples: Squaring an adjacency matrix counts two-step walks between vertices
counterexamples: Interpreting A^k entries as counting only simple paths is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Composition rule expansion
rules.input_form: objects A and B with a valid composition law
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Compose structured objects when composition preconditions are satisfied.
examples: Function and operator compositions require compatible codomain-domain interfaces
counterexamples: Composing incompatible objects is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Inverse admissibility expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Introduce inverses only when invertibility conditions are explicitly satisfied.
examples: Matrix inversion requires nonsingularity
counterexamples: Assuming inverses exist without conditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Constraint propagation expansion
rules.input_form: state with constraints C and transform T
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Propagate constraints through each accepted transformation step.
examples: Positivity or boundedness constraints should be preserved or updated after transformation
counterexamples: Dropping constraints silently is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions
